claims.statement: Capex for FY25 expected within INR250 crores including maintenance and additions
R&D investment to continue at 5-6% of sales
Europe business expected to grow 15-20% in FY25
EBITDA margin expected to bounce back to 17-18% over next few years
Q4 FY24 EBITDA margin 13.2% vs 15% YoY; FY24 EBITDA margin 14.6% vs 17.4% YoY
Gross margin decline due to higher sales promotion and digital marketing spend on Sensodent K
Significant Capex undertaken over last 5 years to cater to future growth for next 2-3 years without major incremental capex
Expects Europe business to deliver ~20% CAGR over 5 years and U.S. business ~30% CAGR over next 2 years from FY26
Emerging markets expected to grow 18-20% CAGR for next couple of years
Capex guidance of INR250 crores for FY25 maintained
No major capex expected after current round; only maintenance capex going forward
Expects to borrow additional INR100 crores beyond cash flows to meet capex commitments
Other expenses expected to stabilize at INR110-120 crores per quarter going forward
Gross margin decline due to U.S. supply shortfall (~INR20 crores) and shift of Sensodent-K/KF cosmetic variants to subsidiary
Transition from out-licensing to front-end U.S. model compressing near-term margins but improving recurring margin profile
European business has very healthy order book position; expects maximum benefit from master manufacturing plan completion by end of Q2
Warren Remedies investing ~INR100 crores in API facility at AURIC to more than double API business; validation and approvals expected in 6-8 months
Oral care D2C facility at AURIC built with ~INR100 crores capex; one line operational, space for two more
Goa Plant 2 sterile lines remediation to be completed by October; full potential supply expected thereafter
Most plant corrections to complete in Q2; consistent U.S. supply expected from Q3
Master manufacturing plan underway across sites with automation, upgradation, capacity increase for efficiency
11 manufacturing facilities (7 FDF, 4 API)
R&D facility with 400+ scientists
Management declined to give forward guidance, preferring to wait one more quarter
Capex guidance for FY25 is INR200+ crores, with INR180 crores already incurred in H1
Incremental capex for H2 FY25 expected to be minimal
Capex primarily for plant upgradation under master manufacturing plan, sterile plant upgrades, and advances for new injectable and ophthalmic lines
Master manufacturing plan aims to increase output by 50% per site, increase batch sizes, reduce testing costs and process times
Europe sites: one done, second almost complete; emerging market site almost done; US sterile plant remediation expected to finish by Q3 FY25
US sterile plant: one line up now, one line every 15 days; four lines total
Order book for US and Europe is very healthy
EBITDA margin 13.4% in Q2 FY25 vs 15.6% YoY; PAT margin INR128M vs INR331M YoY; gross margin impact due to fixed operating costs at plants under shutdown and product mix shift
Raw material prices trending down slightly; benefit to reflect in next couple of quarters
Order book for international formulations business to Europe and US stands at about INR180 crores
US will stay partly impacted in Q4 due to warning letter; EU should be back on its feet; API, India domestic sales and services expected to go all out
Plant I master manufacturing plan completed in Q3; regular supplies impact seen in Q4; Baddi rollout ongoing with 1 month loss in Q4
EBITDA margin for Q3 FY25 at 5.5% (INR201 million) vs 14.6% (INR653 million) YoY; 9-month average down to 10.5-11%
Previously confident of maintaining 13-14% EBITDA for FY25 but that has gone for a toss; expect to work back slowly
Expect improvement on geographical business basis in Q4; India business per head yield should improve; other expenses to come under control
Do not expect to come back to 15% EBITDA before Q3 FY26; possibly by Q3 FY26 could start seeing early signs of 13%
Europe growth expected close to 15% at least for FY26/FY27
Incurred close to INR200 crores this year including new machines, upgradation, projects, advances; line upgradation more repairs and maintenance than capex
Capex includes new unit at Auric for cosmetic toothpaste, API capacity block, newer equipment for solid oral efficiency
Target fixed asset turnover at least 2x
Management expects consolidated losses to have bottomed out in Q4 FY25 with improvement from Q2 FY26 onwards
Europe business expected to return to INR300 crore level in FY26
Warren Remedies OTC business expected to breakeven in FY27
Other expenses targeted to be arrested at INR120 crores per quarter from current INR140 crores
Capex for FY26 limited to routine maintenance only, major capex work at finishing stage
Additional depreciation of INR9-10 crores per annum from new asset capitalization in FY26
Master manufacturing plan completed 99%, enabling 2.5x revenue potential from international business
Solid oral manufacturing sites restructured to reduce complexity, increase batch sizes, and cut 25% fewer batches for same output
Sufficient orders in hand for international business to utilize restructured manufacturing capacity
Consolidated EBITDA margin dropped to 6% in FY25 from 13.7% in FY24 due to manufacturing shutdowns and warning letter impact
Standalone EBITDA margin fell to 8.6% in FY25 from 14.6% in FY24
Management expects quarter-on-quarter EBITDA improvement from Q1 FY26 onwards and aims to return to 11-13% EBITDA levels seen in prior years.
Remediation at Goa Plant-2 expected to be mostly complete by August 2025, with FDA inspection possible from September 2025.
Master manufacturing program Phase-1 rolled out in Q1 FY26; all plants expected operational by end of Q2 FY26, with full efficiency visible in Phase-2 from Q3 FY26.
Capex for FY26 expected to be around Rs. 50 crore incrementally, focused on completing ongoing projects at Goa Plant-2 and Warren Remedies API site.
R&D spend expected to be maintained at 5-5.5% of sales; 4-5 product filings planned for FY26.
Debt repayment of Rs. 68 crore planned over remaining 9 months of FY26 after Rs. 21 crore repaid in Q1.
Sterile product supply to US from Goa Plant-2 expected to show impact by Q3 FY26 after FDA allowed restart of 2 of 4 lines.
European business expected to bounce back to regular supply levels by Q3 FY26 after supply challenges resolve by end of Q2.
Warren Remedies OTC business expected to take a couple of years to reach EBITDA breakeven; Q1 FY26 was EBITDA positive.
Standalone EBITDA margin improved to 3.9% in Q1 FY26 from 1% in Q4 FY25; consolidated EBITDA margin improved to 4.1% from negative in Q4 FY25.
Remediation costs continue at ~Rs. 4 crore per quarter for Goa Plant-2.
International solid oral exports grew >26% QoQ in Q1 FY26 due to master manufacturing program Phase-1 rollout.
US formulation revenue declined to Rs. 283 million from Rs. 487 million YoY; Europe revenue declined to Rs. 635 million from Rs. 754 million YoY.
Goa Plant-2: US FDA allowed manufacturing restart on 2 of 4 lines; European authorities approved sterile product supply from the plant.
Master manufacturing program: 3 of 4 plants fully operational in Phase-1; all 4 expected by end of Q2 FY26.
Management expects consolidated other expenses to be held at INR150-160 crore levels, though likely to stay elevated due to USFDA remediation costs for another 2 quarters.
Management expects double-digit growth in Europe/UK business going forward following MMP completion and customer approvals.
Management targets INR3,500 crore revenue in 3 years (by FY28/FY29), delayed from earlier INR5,000 crore target for FY27.
Management expects maintenance capex of INR50-70 crore per year for next 2-3 years, totaling less than INR150 crore over 3 years.
Management plans to repay INR52 crore in H2 FY26 and INR140 crore in FY27.
Management expects R&D spend to reduce from ~5% of sales to 4% in the first year as sales pick up.
Standalone EBITDA margin improved to 12.4% in Q2 FY26 from 3.8% in Q1 FY26, but down from 13.4% YoY.
Consolidated EBITDA margin improved to 9.1% in Q2 FY26 from 4.1% in Q1 FY26, but down from 9.3% YoY.
Domestic formulation business EBITDA margin estimated at 20-25% by management.
Received final ANDA approval from USFDA for Rivaroxaban tablets.
USFDA completed inspection of API manufacturing facility at Patalganga with 0 observations.
Clarity Pharma (UK distributor) launched 4-5 products; management expects revenue update by March.
Two restarted sterile lines at Goa Plant 2 have completed media fills; minimal manufacturing started; USFDA acknowledged readiness.
Largest sterile line (Line 1) at Goa still not approved by USFDA; only 2 of 4 lines operational.
Sale and leaseback of Waluj plant equipment for ~INR50 crore in H1 FY26.
Generation 2 capex of INR200 crore deferred; evaluating CMO model vs in-house investment for US market.
Europe revenue expected to grow 20%+ annually over next few years with margin improvement
Europe revenue could reach INR400-500 crores by FY28-29
FPP US portfolio expects at least 5 new product launches in FY27
Warren Remedies OTC business expected to grow at least 30% next year
Consolidated other expenses targeted at INR150 crores per quarter
Long-term debt to reduce to ~INR550-555 crores by March 2026
Maintenance capex of INR35-40 crores per annum for next 2-3 years
Consolidated EBITDA margin at 7.3% in Q3 FY26 vs 3% YoY
Gross margin improved ~300 bps sequentially due to better subsidiary performance and portfolio mix
Target to stabilize at 13-14% EBITDA margin in next couple of years
Europe YTD revenue INR167 crores; Q4 expected to be much better due to MMP Phase II approvals
Patalganga API site received EIR with zero 483s from USFDA
Auric API block ready for validation batches; commercial supply pending USFDA/EU qualification
Goa Plant II sterile lines restarted but meaningful contribution pending USFDA audit
Total Capital Expenditure (Standalone) Rs 41.1 crore
Capital Work in Progress - Goa II-Line V and VI upgradation/new line
Capital Work in Progress - Energy saving projects at Goa and Baddi
Capital Work in Progress - Goa II-Effluent/Sewage treatment plant
Capital Work in Progress - Warren Remedies Private Limited
Debt repayment of INR 140 crore per year for next 3 years (FY27, FY28, FY29) with target to prepay more
No major capex planned for next 2 years
Standalone EBITDA margin 14.7% in Q4 FY26 vs 1% YoY and 6.6% QoQ; Consolidated EBITDA margin 10.9% vs -0.2% YoY and 7.3% QoQ
Decent order book in place for international business; Europe business scaling with customer approvals mostly completed
Aiming for double-digit EBITDA margins for FY27
Standalone EBITDA margin expanded to 10.3% in Q1 FY27 from 3.8% a year ago
Gross margin impacted by ~200 bps due to higher COGS from war-related material shortages and price increases
Expect COGS pressure to partly continue into Q2 FY27 and normalize after Q3 FY27
Consolidated other expenses expected below INR150 crores, currently around INR110-120 crores
Europe order book exceeds INR250 crores for execution
FY27 capex limited to maintenance, not exceeding INR40-50 crores
Goa Plant I at 70-80% utilization on single shift; Baddi Unit I at 70-80%; Baddi Unit III at 70-75%
Domestic formulations growth guidance maintained at high single-digit for FY27 despite Q2 headwinds
Regulated markets export growth target of 20%+ for next 1-2 years
International formulations expected to deliver decent double-digit growth for FY27
R&D spend capped at 5% of topline, currently at 4% YTD
Capex for physical assets limited to Rs 25 crore for FY27
Consolidated EBITDA margin at 9.2% in Q2 FY27 vs 9.1% YoY and 8.8% QoQ
Gross margins impacted by ~30% increase in COGS, raw materials, freight, solvents in Q2 FY27
Regulated markets revenue grew 21.1% YoY to Rs 1,109 million in Q2 FY27
US formulations revenue grew 16.4% YoY to Rs 391 million in Q2 FY27
Europe formulations revenue grew 23.5% YoY to Rs 675 million in Q2 FY27
API revenue grew 4.6% YoY to Rs 451 million in Q2 FY27
CRO and analytical services revenue grew 20.8% YoY to Rs 82 million in Q2 FY27
Goa Plant-1 cleared MHRA audit; AnaCipher CRO cleared ANVISA inspection
US FDA inspection outcome for Goa plant expected by first week of December
US FDA audit for Warren API plant expected by Q2 FY28
Current infrastructure can support 4x international formulations revenue
